memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Moses went back to Jethro his father-in-law and said to him, "Let me return to my own people in Egypt to see if any of them are still alive." Jethro said, "Go, and I wish you well." Now the Lord had said to Moses in Midian, "Go back to Egypt, for all those who wanted to kill you are dead."" - Exodus 4:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses has just met God at a burning bush. He could have simply packed up and left. Instead, he goes to his father-in-law and asks permission to leave.

There is real grace in this. Jethro had taken in a homeless fugitive, given him work, a family, and forty years of shelter. Moses does not treat a divine calling as licence to walk out on human obligations.

We sometimes use spiritual language to escape ordinary responsibilities. God's calling never releases us from courtesy, gratitude, or the duties we have taken on. Paul told Timothy that anyone who does not provide for his own household has denied the faith (1 Tim 5:8). Spirituality that ignores people is not spirituality.

Then God adds a quiet reassurance: those who wanted to kill you are dead. The fear that drove Moses out of Egypt forty years ago no longer applies. Circumstances change. Some of what we still fear belongs to a chapter God has already closed.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I using spiritual busyness to avoid an ordinary responsibility?
2. What old fear am I carrying that no longer actually exists?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to honour the people You have placed over and around me. Free me from fears that belong to a closed chapter. Amen.
